Row predicates over an event's columns

Source: R/lang_v2.R
omop_where.Rd

omop_where() captures an R expression as data (it is never evaluated) using the closed grammar ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, %in%, is.na(), !, &, | and parentheses, with literal numbers, strings (ISO dates are strings), logical constants and concept IDs. Several arguments are combined with AND. Bare names are column names; the normalised value of an event is value. Logic is three-valued as in SQL: a comparison with a NULL column is UNKNOWN and only TRUE rows are kept.

Usage

omop_where(...)

omop_where_tree(tree)

Arguments

...

Predicate expressions (unevaluated).

tree

A predicate tree.

Value

An omop_predicate object.

Details

A parameter placeholder, omop_param(...) written inline with literal arguments, may stand for any literal; it is the only call ever evaluated (alone, in the caller's frame) and is bound before emission.

omop_where_tree() takes the explicit tree form of the plan schema (list(var =, op =, value =) leaves, and/or lists, not), which also offers between.

Examples

omop_where(value >= 6.5)
omop_where(!is.na(value), unit_concept_id %in% c(8554, 8753))
omop_where_tree(list(var = "value", op = "between",
                     value = list(lower = 5, upper = 10)))
